newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends lower on bearish stock data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends lower on bearish stock data.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex ended lower Wednesday on a sharp decline in heating oil after an inventory report showed a bearish stock build in heat and high production levels for distillate, traders and analysts said.
"Today heating oil just brought the whole market down. We followed whatever heat did," said a trader.
November heating oil ended 2.49 cents lower at 70.96 cents a gallon after falling as low as 70.70 cents.
December crude ended the day 67 cents a barrel lower at $24.86 while November gasoline settled 0.96 cent lower at 68.16 cents a gallon.
The American Petreoleum Institute (API) reported heat stocks grew 2.4 million barrels for the week ended October 18.

Much of the build was concentrated in the U.S. northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world. Heating oil prices have risen steeply in the last several months since inventories were at record low levels.
The API said distillate inventories overall, which includes both diesel and heating oil, were about unchanged.
But, traders said a record high distillate production rate of 3.7 million barrels a day was a market focus and indicated stocks would increase.
Meanwhile, Colonial Pipeline Co on Monday said it received a surge in requests to ship distillates, especially heating oil, on its huge pipeline that runs from Houston to the New York Harbor.
"Basically this means that there is plenty of barrels of distillate available to be shipped to the Northeast," said Linda Abramo, analyst with Energy Security Analysis Inc.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
